findings.title: Migration raises NoMethodError when `embed_category` setting row is absent
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. `site_settings` only contains rows for settings that have been explicitly changed, and the join additionally requires the stored value to still match a category *name*. For the overwhelming majority of installs (default `embed_category` of `''`, or a renamed/deleted category) the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration and therefore any upgrade. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern is used on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. Both lookups need to handle the empty-result case.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted unnormalized, so embedding silently stops working after upgrade
findings.body: Host values are copied straight from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting with raw SQL, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` which strips the scheme and path. The old setting legitimately contained values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (see the removed specs in spec/models/site_setting_spec.rb). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI(referer).host` (e.g. `discourse.org`) against the stored `host` column, so rows containing `http://discourse.org` will never match and previously-working embeds start raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess` after the upgrade. The migration must normalize each value (strip scheme/path) before inserting.

findings.title: Host value interpolated directly into INSERT statement
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates a value taken from the database (the old `embeddable_hosts` setting, which was free-form admin input) into SQL without quoting. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration (and could execute arbitrary SQL). Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized insert.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table, and the migration is not reversible
findings.body: `force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so re-running this migration (or running it on a database that already has an `embeddable_hosts` table, e.g. created by a plugin) silently destroys existing rows. In addition, the body is defined in `change` but contains `execute` statements (data copy and `DELETE FROM site_settings`), which Rails cannot reverse: `rake db:rollback` will drop the table without restoring the deleted site settings. Use `def up` (plus an explicit `down`) and drop `force: true`.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is executed unconditionally in `before_validation`. If `host` is nil — e.g. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` which may be missing — validation blows up with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` (and add a presence validation). Note also that `sub!` mutates the string in place, which mutates the caller's/params' string object; `sub` with assignment would be safer.

findings.title: Case-insensitive host lookup compares against a non-downcased value
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the column but not the argument. Host names in a `Referer` header are case-insensitive and browsers/servers may send mixed case (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/page`), in which case `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'` never matches and a legitimately allowed host is rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. Pass `host.downcase`.

findings.title: Host validation regex rejects valid hosts and allows unmatchable ones
findings.body: The format regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` at the end, which rejects hosts admins can legitimately want to embed from: single-label hosts (`localhost`), TLDs longer than 5 characters (`example.engineering`, `example.technology`), and IP addresses. Conversely the regex permits an optional `:port`, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI(...).host`, which never contains a port, so a saved host like `example.com:3000` can never match a referer and silently never allows anything. The old `host_list` site setting had no such restrictions, so this is a functional regression.

findings.title: update/destroy crash with 500 when the id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which does `nil.host = ...` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`; both raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 response. These endpoints should respond 404 (e.g. `find_by!`/`raise Discourse::NotFound`) for unknown ids.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that pretends to save
findings.body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores the request body entirely and just re-renders the current state, so the route registered in config/routes.rb (`put "customize/embedding"`) silently discards any submitted data while returning 200. The admin controller's `saveChanges` action (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 line 6) calls `embedding.update({})` against it, though nothing in embedding.hbs triggers that action. Either implement the update or remove the route/action so the API does not advertise behaviour it does not have.

findings.title: `*_ids` hydration deletes the ids even when the sideloaded collection is missing
findings.body: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, any key matching `(.+)_ids` is now replaced: `obj[pluralize(subType)] = obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and `delete obj[k]` is executed unconditionally. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes the key when hydration succeeded), this means that for any REST-serialized payload containing an `*_ids` array that is not sideloaded in the root, the original ids are lost and the model gets an array full of `undefined`. Also, if the server sends `null` for such a key, `obj[k].map` throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'map' of null`. (`hydrated || []` on the next line is dead code since `map` always returns an array.) Only replace the key when every lookup resolves, and guard against non-array values.

findings.title: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces a single occurrence, so `basePath` normalizes `embeddable_host` correctly but a type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_admin_model`) still fails the `ADMIN_MODELS` lookup and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `/_/g` (or `Ember.String.dasherize`).

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The two file bodies were clearly pasted into the wrong files; this makes the fabricators undiscoverable by filename and will confuse anyone touching category fabrication.

findings.title: New mutating admin endpoints have no behavioural tests
findings.body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. There is no coverage for `create`/`update`/`destroy` (including the default-to-uncategorized behaviour, the 500-on-missing-record paths noted above, invalid host handling) nor for access control (non-admin/anonymous requests). The same applies to spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb, which does not exercise `show`/`update` at all. Given these endpoints create the data that gates framing/embedding (a security-relevant allowlist), they should be tested.

findings.title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all (the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check was removed), so this example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for a fabricated topic — not because no host exists. The name is now misleading and the example asserts nothing about hosts; it should be renamed/removed.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two `EmbeddableHost` rows with the same host (the migration creates no unique index either, and `before_validation` normalizes `http://example.com` and `example.com` to the same value). `record_for_host` then arbitrarily takes `.first`, so an admin editing the category of a duplicated host can see no effect on which category embedded topics are created in. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and/or a unique index.
